1: # Dolt federation: BDPv4 implementation plan
2: 
3: Author: Codex. Date: 2026-11-10. Status: proposed planning baseline; implementation readiness remains gated by Ph0 evidence. Independent review results are retained under docs/receipts/hv. No implementation, package installation, schema migration, data migration or federation activation has occurred.
4: 
5: Architecture authority: [Dolt federation architecture](2026-11-10-federation-dolt-architecture.md). Workflow evidence and requirement inventory: [three-system walkthrough](2026-11-10-federation-three-system-workflows.md). This plan replaces the old forwarding/read-switch execution sequence for versioned federation. Retain the October and earlier November drafts as historical evidence, not competing instructions.
6: 
7: ## 1. Scope and acceptance
8: 
9: The logical peers H, A and B must independently edit and commit the same logical project's data, exchange committed histories through the hub, preserve uncommitted work and branches, and review conflicts without pull requests. Add Dolt as a fourth supported database and provide a safe migration tool from SQLite, PostgreSQL and SQL Server. Existing providers and explicit DirectProxy remain supported. The second node is the isolated FED-ATLAS-B test peer; real-host acceptance uses LAB and LEGION, with the three-peer fixture provisioned in Ph0.
10: 
11: Success is demonstrated by every workflow U01-U15, every linked FR/TR/TEST criterion, all supported provider regressions and three-system restart/recovery tests. An empty control table is insufficient proof: compare accepted commit ancestry, project data and branch state, including pending drafts/reviews. Source-code Git, arbitrary file synchronization, PRs, automatic hub election, live cross-provider CDC and concurrent independent schema migrations are outside this release.
12: 
13: ## 2. Fastest dependency sequence
14: 
15: Phase identifiers are Ph0 through Ph8; they do not denote priority levels.
16: 
17: 1. Ph0: prove Dolt/EF10/provider/remote fit before investing in integration.
18: 2. Ph1: add fourth provider and separate schema migration assembly; preserve original providers.
19: 3. Ph2: split project-versioned and operational storage, branch-scoped access and editing ownership.
20: 4. Ph3: deliver seed migration, audit-backfill preparation and verified all-domain project recovery export; keep targets isolated.
21: 5. Ph4: expose explicit commits, branch/history/diff and local publication intent.
22: 6. Ph5: implement enrollment, guarded remote publication and the hub table/poller.
23: 7. Ph6: implement safe receiving, reviewed merges, join migration and end-to-end crash/restore recovery.
24: 8. Ph7: expose complete client/MCP/REPL/plugin workflows and user-visible status.
25: 9. Ph8: run two-real-host acceptance plus a named three-logical-peer fixture, then prepare a staged lab cutover under DEPLOY HOLD.
26: 
27: Prepare test fixtures, DTO/API documentation and plugin contract fixtures during earlier phases where independent, but do not move unfinished implementation past a Byrd gate. Provider feasibility, not old forwarding fixes, is now the critical path. Reuse existing identity, diagnostics, provider abstractions, audit and typed clients; replace forwarding/command-replay paths only for versioned projects.
28: 
29: ## 3. Source-control and donor handling
30: 
31: Create an isolated integration worktree from the current accepted develop when implementation is authorized. Suggested branch `integration/federation-dolt-20261110`; use separate small phase PRs against it. Preserve all existing worktrees and unrelated working-tree edits. Do not create or clean worktrees merely to write this plan.
32: 
33: The prior PR83/P1.5 work is a donor only for applicable security, identity, cross-platform path and regression fixes. Verify each current diff and test before porting. Do not merge old backfill, forwarding, read-switch or custom database synchronization machinery wholesale. C4 p4/*, namespace/analyzer work and historical worktree cleanup are not dependencies. Preserve explicit existing legacy modes through their named regression contracts; they do not authorize LocalProxy forwarding for versioned projects.
34: 
35: ## 4. Byrd gate contract
36: 
37: For each small slice, first define the acceptance cases, fixtures and negative controls. Prove every required assertion passes against correct controlled mocks and rejects deliberately wrong behavior as expected negative controls inside a passing harness. Establish zero failures, zero skips and no unexecuted required cases before production implementation. Then implement the smallest behavior and bind the same cases, inputs, assertions and interaction checks to the real implementation; remediate until the production-bound and full applicable exit gates pass. A deliberately red production suite is not the mock gate. Mocks must exercise the asserted orchestration boundary.
38: 
39: Use targeted `./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups '<project>:<class>' --test-run-id '<phase-slice>'` after changes. At each phase exit run the entire current-plus-prior unit suite once with `./build.ps1 Test`, requiring zero failures and zero skips. `./build.ps1 Compile` and `./build.ps1 ValidateTraceability` are mandatory gate commands. Add real-container integration tests where a mock cannot prove SQL, migration, locking or remote semantics. Do not broaden/repeat a passing gate without changes or new evidence requiring it. Receipts include SHA/tree state, image/package versions, commands, TRX, fail/skip counts, AC mapping and negative controls.
40: 
41: The proposed test-class names below are implementation targets, not claims they exist today. Register new projects/classes in Nuke discovery as part of their owning phase. Do not add skipped placeholders for later phases; keep deferred coverage in requirements/TODO state. New federation test projects target xUnit v3 and use its native skip (Assert.Skip, Assert.SkipWhen, Assert.SkipUnless); no Xunit.SkippableFact or v2 xunit packages, per MEMORY-BESTPRACTICE-001 section 10.
42: 
43: Retain the operator's complete phase-exit gate on both LAB and LEGION: Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, the full Build.Tests suite, and ValidateTraceability at the same accepted head. Test currently excludes Build.Tests; do not infer its coverage from a green Test receipt. Ph0 records the complete discovered Build.Tests class inventory and its Nuke TestGroups invocation; every listed class and test must execute, with zero failures and zero skips. MigrationIntegrationTests and the new TestFederationProviders suite are complementary and neither replaces the other. Keep unit, integration and build-suite receipts distinct and run the full set once per final phase head, repeating only after changes or failed gates.
44: 
45: Add Nuke target `TestFederationProviders` with the planned command `./build.ps1 TestFederationProviders --providers sqlite,postgresql,sqlserver,dolt --test-run-id '<phase>-providers'`. It is not an existing command today. Ph0 records exact PostgreSQL/SQL Server/Dolt image versions and digests and the SQLite package version; Ph1 implements the target and refuses missing/unhealthy containers as a gate failure, never a skip. Every Ph1-Ph8 exit requires both the full unit gate and this real-provider/remote suite with zero failures and zero skips. Container-dependent classes are registered only in TestFederationProviders and excluded from Test by category at discovery, never runtime skipping. Receipts include image digests and environment readiness evidence.
46: 
47: ## 5. Ph0: feasibility and exact dependency selection
48: 
49: Deliver a version-pinned compatibility receipt and license/dependency record for Dolt and the MySQL-protocol EF provider and driver selected under B1. Use current net10.0/EF10.0.0 as the baseline. Read the dependency compliance rules before additions. Existing Dolt EF samples establish possibility, not compatibility.
50: 
51: Prove on LAB Linux and LEGION native Windows against real databases (containers where appropriate): full current model creation; representative CRUD/LINQ/raw SQL; concurrency tokens; transaction rollback; decimal/date/text/index/FK mappings; migrations; branch connection isolation; explicit SQL commit versus Dolt commit; merge conflicts/constraints; clean and dirty remote pushes; lost responses; authenticated project isolation; inability to bypass guarded publication through raw remote requests. Verify canonical-ref advancement and remote recovery under process death. Compare candidate clean merges against domain validators.
52: 
53: Classes: `DoltProviderCompatibilityTests`, `DoltRemoteAuthorizationTests`, `DoltBranchIsolationTests`, `DoltCommitBoundaryTests`. Red conditions: unsupported mappings/query translation, ordinary SaveChanges creating history, pool branch leakage, unauthorized ref mutation or missing recovery guarantees. Green: all named contracts pass on pinned versions using the operator-accepted EF10 provider or patched community fork under B1, with no bespoke from-scratch provider or custom merge engine.
54: 
55: Ph0 runs a disposable harness and records exact commands, digests, TRX and fail/skip counts. Ph1 carries the proven Ph0 contract assertions into maintained classes under TestFederationProviders and passes them at Ph1 exit. If Ph0 changes repository code, the full Test gate also applies at Ph0 exit; disposable prototypes do not become an undocumented production dependency.
56: 
57: Ph0 exit consists of the following numbered **blocking outputs**. The implementation owner produces each evidence record; the operator accepts it, with independent HV selected under section 14 and current Global reviewer policy, assessing substantive accuracy/completeness. Each record stores owner, status (unproven/proven/accepted), evidence paths and dependent phases. Initial status for all B1-B12 is unproven. Every B1-B12 receipt has separate LAB and LEGION evidence rows; Windows is not inferred from Linux. Ph0 verifies the current-scope coverage index and binds each applicable acceptance criterion and workflow to its implementation phase. All must be accepted before Ph1 production integration begins; Ph0 prototypes remain disposable.
58: 
59: 1. B1: exact provider/driver/image versions, digests, licenses and all-four-provider fixture versions; LAB /var/lib/dolt mount and native LEGION hosting inventory. Verify actual Windows service name/account/executable/start/recovery policy, data ACLs and child-process lifecycle before accepting the proposed host. If absent or unsuitable, obtain approval for a concrete supported alternative (Ph1-Ph8).
60: 2. B2: every entity, relationship, interactive/automatic writer and auto-updated column; session capture remains operational and only explicit promoted snapshots become versioned (Ph2-Ph8).
61: 3. B3: full standalone McpDbContext versus Dolt-only project/control context topology, additive migration chains and cross-database soft-reference validators (Ph1-Ph3).
62: 4. B4: exact ID grammar per generated/human-assigned family, legacy compatibility, sort/display, parser/plugin/traceability changes and restored allocator behavior (Ph2-Ph8).
63: 5. B5: exact restored Duende 7.4 patch version and matching source-tag/API references, with issuance/introspection/revocation tests on that package (v8 documentation is insufficient); existing IdentityServer client-per-node/owner binding, reference tokens and scopes, gateway introspection/revocation, backend-only Dolt credentials, enforceable remote publication permissions and credential containment, worker-only remote procedures, gated worker live-branch mutation path and rotation/revocation (Ph2/Ph5-Ph8).
64: 6. B6: real merge/constraint/conflict-transaction semantics, retained review evidence, safe conflict persistence including whether `dolt_allow_commit_conflicts` is needed, and unrelated-history behavior. Never enable unresolved conflicts on live project branches (Ph4-Ph6).
65: 7. B7: single-author schema distribution, startup migration exclusion, expand/contract rules, mandatory pre-binary-swap draft disposition, all-local-branch attestation/fencing, offline old-schema commits and feature catch-up, worker protocol negotiation (Ph1/Ph3/Ph5/Ph6/Ph8).
66: 8. B8: seed/join/recovery-export manifest, audit backfill, duplicate detection and permanent aliases, one common root, mandatory legacy-divergence review over B2-classified versioned columns after canonical normalization; reviewed scoped rules may expand to enumerated per-row decisions with no wildcard default. Include identity/deletion accounting, canonical hashes, immutable migration-commit plus final-main verification and closed-until-integrated cutover (Ph3 seed/export, Ph6 join, Ph8 acceptance).
67: 9. B9: single writer ownership, write gate/fence transitions including every worker live-branch mutation, working-set hash API, requestId commit trailers and crash reconciliation (Ph2/Ph4-Ph6).
68: 10. B10: measured fixture-scale storage/latency/history growth, resource budgets and explicit operating limits; no unsupported throughput/SLA claim (Ph1/Ph5/Ph8).
69: 11. B11: polling/retry/stale-branch and15minute/24hour review-age thresholds, subscription-state schema and monotonic generation/epoch semantics (Ph5/Ph7).
70: 12. B12: local/remote candidate/review refs, GC/retention, hub-restore epoch/reconciliation, network loopback isolation, named CA/pins and secret-safe receipts, plus secret-detection and disclosure response (Ph4-Ph8).
71: 
72: Per the operator decision of 2026-11-11 (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-002; architecture section 8), a prerelease or community-fork EF10 provider, patched by this project and contributed upstream as needed, is an accepted dependency for the Dolt project context, so the absence of a GA-maintained provider does not block B1. If no EF10 provider can be made to drive Dolt's required semantics even with reasonable patching, report concrete options for approval; do not downgrade the repository silently or ship a bespoke from-scratch provider without the operator's agreement. This plan is executable through Ph0 but is not implementation-ready for later slices until these evidence-dependent choices are locked.
73: 
74: ## 6. Ph1: fourth provider and schema migrations
75: 
76: Requirements: FR-MCP-186. Extend `McpDatabaseProviderKind`, `McpDatabaseProviderFactory`, `McpDbContextFactory`, runtime options/configuration validation, health output and setup tooling with canonical `dolt`. Add `DoltMcpDatabaseProviderStrategy` and `QBrainAi.Storage.DoltMigrations`, with provider-specific snapshot/baseline. Never edit existing migrations; add migrations only where B3 requires. Include provider selections in build/package/admin surfaces. Exclude versioned project databases from automatic startup migration; standalone/control contexts retain their approved migration path.
77: 
78: Classes: `DoltProviderResolutionTests`, `DoltMigrationTests`, `FourProviderContractTests`. Include VersionedProjectNotMigratedAtStartup in this owning phase. First prove unknown-provider rejection, unchanged defaults and distinct migration assembly selection. Real-provider tests cover empty database creation, baseline-to-next upgrade, interrupted startup/retry, idempotent reapplication, schema drift detection and application CRUD after upgrade. Test all original providers for regression. No production data copy in this phase.
79: 
80: ## 7. Ph2: project routing, data boundaries and editing ownership
81: 
82: Requirements: FR-MCP-174,176,177,182,184,185,189. Add immutable ProjectId/local-path enrollment mapping, per-project provider selection, project and control contexts, full table classification, branch-scoped DbContext/query/index keys, local ID allocation and fenced edit leases. A versioned project's ordinary requests must never enter LocalProxy forwarding. Preserve DirectProxy behavior for explicit legacy configuration; no ambiguous combination on one project.
83: 
84: Fold MCP-FEDIDENTITY-001 owner binding and user-management requirements into this phase. Audit/outbox storage remains unversioned, but its delivery obligation is hub-bound, not local-only. Define scoped permanent aliases and local provisional IDs; host paths and credentials remain local. Classes: `FederationLocalExecutionTests`, `ProjectBranchContextTests`, `FederationDataBoundaryTests`, `NodeTaggedIdentityTests`, `BranchEditLeaseTests`. Cases include BackgroundWritersDoNotDirtyVersionedBranch, SecondAgentLoggingNeedsNoLease, LegacyIdsRemainValid and LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected. Red: offline request waits for hub, cross-project row visible, secret or branchable audit in clone, duplicate IDs after branch/restart, pooled connection changes branch, or one agent commits another's work. Green: local read-after-write/restart, complete entity/writer classification, no branch/project leakage, safe expired-lease recovery and stable replicated IDs. Provider schema changes introduced here require migrations for each affected supported provider, not Dolt alone.
85: 
86: LeaseLostDuringWriteRejected means admission after expiry/fence change is rejected and takeover waits for an already-admitted transaction; it does not demand aborting a transaction legitimately holding the gate through completion.
87: 
88: ## 8. Ph3: seed migration and project recovery export
89: 
90: Requirements: FR-MCP-187, FR-MCP-182/184, FR-MCP-AUDIT-001 and the reconciled backfill contracts. Implement the shared migration planner, immutable source manifest, duplicate-candidate review, permanent alias mapping, seed-only run/resume/verify/status/abort and frozen-head Dolt-to-new-SQLite project export. Audit backfill preparation accounts for every historical TODO/generic audit row; actual hub delivery/receipt binding joins Ph5. Ph3 never invokes publication or reviewed join functionality that does not yet exist.
91: 
92: Classes: MigrationPlannerTests, MigrationResumeTests, MigrationIdentityMappingTests, MigrationVerificationTests, ThreeProviderToDoltMigrationTests, TodoRecoveryExportTests and ProjectRecoveryExportTests. Reuse TEST-MCP-235's exact Given/When/Then cases. SeedPhaseRejectsJoin returns HTTP 501 unsupported_capability with no writes when mode=join is requested. ThreeSourceProviderRoundTrip covers SQLite,PostgreSQL,SQL Server fixtures; both live lab sources are SQLite. DoltTodoExportPreservesNewWrites proves a post-cutover TODO and its child/link/alias graph survive export while retained source bytes remain unchanged. FullProjectRecoveryPreservesAllDomains additionally proves every versioned domain, unpublished branch and dirty working set survives per-branch SQLite export plus the retained Dolt archive; operational stores are backed up at the same quiescence boundary and audit is reconciled. A missing domain or branch blocks routing changes. Same-work/different-ID candidates require review; never rewrite historical text references.
93: 
94: Migration acceptance also covers multi-project separation, soft-deleted rows, decimal/UTC/binary/Unicode edge cases, complete promoted session graphs, hub-bound audit, derived-index rebuild and inert imported operational records. Inject death after target batch commit before acknowledgement, before provider switch and after switch before reopening. Dry-run and failed verification must preserve source bytes and active routing. Ph6 applies the same matrix to joins; source accounting and reviewed-main verification are separate checks.
95: 
96: Exit: disposable seed migrations and verified recovery exports pass all four-provider gates. Keep source SQLite snapshots read-only. No live cutover, join commit, public-ref update or source deletion occurs. Join-specific cases remain planned for Ph6, not skipped tests in Ph3.
97: ## 9. Ph4: explicit history commits and local publication intent
98: 
99: Requirements: FR-MCP-175,177,183,184,189. Implement status/diff/history/commit preview, idempotent explicit commit, branch lifecycle and local unpublished-head scanning. No save hook implicitly creates Dolt history. A hub request cannot auto-commit drafts. Protect preview fingerprints, author provenance and branch edit ownership.
100: 
101: Classes: `FederationCommitTests`, `FederationBranchLifecycleTests`, `PublicationIntentRecoveryTests`. Include CommitRetryReturnsSameHash, CommitPreviewBlocksSecret and StaleBranchReportedNotDeleted. Red: edits trigger sync, commit bundles unauthorized changes, restart loses an unreported commit, or fetched remote commits cause endless republishing. Green: durable explicit commit triggers exactly the needed sync intent, history reconstruction repairs crash windows without duplicate commits, feature publication does not merge main.
102: 
103: ## 10. Ph5: hub control table and publication
104: 
105: Requirements: FR-MCP-176,178,179,181,182,184,185. Provision the hub shared remote separately from its local working copy. Implement enrollment and project/branch subscription, candidate upload/validation/acceptance, expected-head publication, SyncSubscription state-table migrations, polling/reporting, durable receipts, worker epochs and remote-head reconciliation. One row per subscription replaces command-message generations/leases/coalescing. Both nodes initiate communication; H's local worker uses the same authenticated gateway. Add existing IdentityServer clients/scopes, audit/batches ingestion with idempotent receipts, human-ID reservation, restore epoch and polling. Test AuditReachesHub, AuditRetryIdempotent, SimultaneousHumanIdReservation, SqlPortUnreachableAcrossLink and HubRestoreFromOlderBackup. No native remote endpoint is exposed to node credentials.
106: 
107: Classes: `FederationEnrollmentTests`, `FederationPublicationTests`, `FederationControlTableTests`, `FederationPollingTests`. Include LocalAppUserCannotPush, RevokedCredentialFailsFetchAndPublish and OldWorkerEpochCannotReportSuccess. 109: ## 11. Ph6: incoming integration, review, join migration and recovery
110: 
111: Requirements: FR-MCP-178,180,181,186,187,188,189. Implement temporary integration branches, clean-merge validation, dirty-branch deferral, gated live-branch application, conflict review with head-bound resolution, recovery pins/receipts, maintenance preflight/attestation/status and derived-state refresh. Incoming data must not re-execute business commands or external effects. Include IncomingMergeCannotRaceAdmittedEdit, covering an isolated worker that must use the owning server's gate API.

118: ## 12. Ph7: server and plugin workflows
119:

Inventory actual plugin repositories and versions at phase entry; do not edit another plugin through the wrong agent identity. Expose capabilities, project/branch context, status/diff/history/commit/sync, branches, review, audit delivery status, identity enrollment/owner management, human-ID reservation, aliases, admin migration/export commands and maintenance.preflight/attest/status as defined by the architecture and TRs. Each obligation is explicit in the corresponding FR/TR/TEST, not inferred from a generic status command. 124: ## 13. Ph8: two-host acceptance, three-peer fixture and held cutover
125: 
126: Build from the accepted integration SHA. Real-host acceptance requires LAB-OMARCHY(10.42.0.214/Linux) and PAYTON-LEGION2(10.42.0.143/Windows), both starting from retained SQLite copies. It does not depend on an unprovisioned third machine. Separately, Nuke provisions an ephemeral three-logical-peer fixture named FED-ATLAS-H, FED-ATLAS-A and FED-ATLAS-B with isolated databases, loopback dynamic ports and disposable roots under TestResults/{runId}; Ph0 proves that provisioning path on both OSs. These are test processes, never discovered hosts or production enrollment. Execute U01-U15; use H/A for real cross-link tests and the fixture for three-writer interleavings. 998: #### TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010: first-party plugin federation contract contract
999: 
1000: Status: pending. Revision audit amended 2026-11-10.
1001: All plugins call typed server/client/MCP/REPL contracts; no raw SQL/CLI fallback. Status DTO includes projectId, branch, localHead, publishedHead, observedUtc, dirty, ahead, behind, publicationState, incomingTarget, connectivity, reviewCount, oldestReviewAgeSeconds, waitingLocalWorkAgeSeconds, auditPendingCount, hubEpoch, workerEpoch. Capability contract version1 is negotiated; unknown version=409 unsupported_contract. Administrative maintenance.preflight/attest/status and migration commands share the same typed service as Nuke. Stable error envelope={code, message, requestId, projectId, branch, retryable, details}; status codes are locked in the technical contract appendix.
1002: 
1003: Technical contract appendix (TR-MCP-FEDERATION-010): all below routes are under /qbrainai/federation unless the commits route specifies the project/branch path. Every mutation requires requestId UUID and authenticated subject; node network requests additionally carry the project-scoped reference token. Responses carry contractVersion=1 and the stable error envelope. Path/body ProjectId mismatch is403 unauthorized_project. No endpoint accepts credentials in URL, argv or persisted receipts.
1004: 
1005: Read/status routes: GET capabilities returns200 {contractVersion,capabilities}; GET projects/{projectId}/status returns200 the status DTO; GET projects/{projectId}/branches returns200 {items:[{name,head,dirty,publishedHead}]}; GET conflicts and GET conflicts/{reviewId} return200 review records filtered by membership. POST control/poll returns200 {hubEpoch,subscriptions}; reads never acknowledge work. POST control/report validates observed generation and worker epoch, returns200 the durable receipt or409 the named fence error. Poll/report use control scope; reads use read scope.
1006: 
1007: Mutation routes: POST enroll returns201 the enrollment (or200 the same idempotent enrollment); POST projects/{projectId}/branches creates201 {branch,head}; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/select returns200 {sessionId,branch,head} after local lease validation; POST projects/{projectId}/branches/{branch}/commits returns201 {commitHash,publicationState}, or200 the same commit on retry. POST publication/accept returns200 {requestId,hubEpoch,publishedHead,publishedGeneration,receiptId} only after the guarded ref update is durable. POST branches/merge and POST conflicts/{reviewId}/resolve bind expected heads and return201 the new commit; a conflict returns202 {outcome:needs_review,reviewId} while the live head stays unchanged. Share/merge/publication require publish scope plus branch permission. Enrollment requires enroll scope and the operator owner-binding approval.
1008: 
1009: POST audit/batches accepts {requestId,projectId,records:[AuditRecord]}, returns200 {receipts:[{originNodeId,recordId,payloadHash,outcome,receivedUtc}]}, and requires audit scope. Every record must match the token/project and batch ProjectId. Any invalid record rejects the whole batch before insert. Exact duplicate is already_received; payload mismatch is409 audit_id_conflict. POST ids/reservations accepts {requestId,projectId,entityKind,humanId,nodeId}, requires publish scope and returns201 the reservation or200 its exact retry; another owner gets409 human_id_reserved. POST maintenance/preflight and POST maintenance/attest, GET maintenance/status and POST migration/{plan|dry-run|run|resume|verify|export-project|export-todos|cutover|abort}, GET migration/status are operator-only local service operations. They are exposed through typed clients and Nuke, never public node-admin capabilities. A long migration returns202 {migrationId,status}; status/verify return200 a receipt, and a denied readiness check never performs cutover.
1010: 
1011: Stable failure mapping:401 invalid_token;403 unauthorized_project;409 head_changed, working_set_changed, lease_lost, branch_busy, stale_review, stale_worker_epoch, hub_epoch_changed, ambiguous_legacy_id, human_id_reserved, human_id_unreserved, target_not_empty, maintenance_not_ready, migration_source_changed, migration_verification_failed, incompatible_schema, unsupported_contract, publication_required, request_id_conflict, audit_id_conflict and waiting_local_work (the last also a 200 outcome in poll/report; see outcome fields);422 secret_detected, dependency_cycle and unsupported_provider;501 unsupported_capability;503 identity_unavailable or remote_unavailable. TLS rejection produces the local transport code tls_peer_untrusted with no HTTP response and no request sent. Missing required fields return400 invalid_request. Missing authorized resources return404 not_found; project authorization precedes existence disclosure. Malformed/unsupported token is401; valid token lacking project rights is403.
1012: 
1013: Outcome fields are not HTTP errors: committed_locally, already_received, already_applied, waiting_local_work and needs_review remain visible through200 status/report responses (already_applied is the migration-journal idempotency outcome for a rerun completed batch, distinct from the audit-ledger already_received). A requested live mutation blocked by drafts returns409 waiting_local_work; an integration that durably creates review returns202 needs_review. dependency_cycle is a validationErrors entry on that review as well as422 for a directly invalid local mutation. retryable=true is restricted to transient503/transport failures; all stale-head/fence/review errors require reread and a fresh validated action. Idempotent retries with the same requestId but different payload return409 request_id_conflict. No automatic retry creates a different commit.
1014: 
1015: Test fixtures capture actual content hashes as symbols C0,A1,B1,H1,M1,M2,S1 rather than hardcoding unstable engine hashes. Each symbol is immutable within the run manifest. Given/When/Then compares exact hash equality, specified parent sets, row values, status codes and error codes against that manifest; a successful result must never be inferred solely from an empty queue. Capture UTC timestamps and a fake clock for exact15-minute/24-hour age boundaries. All plan phase IDs use Ph0-Ph8; priority values remain separate.
1016: 
1017: Plugin completeness is checked by PluginEnrollmentDiagnostics, PluginRecoveryControls, PluginIdentityDiagnostics, PluginLeastPrivilegeDenial, PluginEffectBoundary and PluginEditingOwnership in their mapped contracts. Ph7 owns their plugin bindings; earlier phases own server behavior. Standalone and explicit DirectProxy compatibility remain under FR-MCP-077/TR-MCP-FED-001; this does not reinstate versioned LocalProxy forwarding.
1018: 
1019: **Acceptance Criteria:**
1020: - [ ] ac-EveryPluginUsesSameContract: Given one fixture for commit R1, conflict R2 and migration R3, when each installed first-party plugin calls its wrapper, then normalized IDs, heads, error codes and audit agent identity match the typed client result.

item.text: Profile reload acknowledged. I am re-running the complete add-profile workflow now, including every eligible profile Markdown file and fresh live Global and McpServer Workspace memories, before resuming the active R2 validation.

---
name: add-profile
description: Load Payton's operator profile into the current session and synthesize active operating guidance from identity, standing preferences, current-session corrections, and project context. Use when the user says add profile, /add-profile, load my profile, remember who I am, after context loss or compaction, or when trust needs to be re-established.
---

## Action

Load the global operator profile and all current Global and active Workspace MCP memories, then turn them into an active operating model for the rest of the session. This is not a summary task. It is a context-recovery and trust-calibration task.

The profile is GLOBAL. It lives in `~/.claude/profile/` and applies in every session and every repo. It does not depend on the active project's `memory/` directory.

## Read Contract

1. Read this `SKILL.md` in full before acting.
2. Read every markdown file in `~/.claude/profile/` in full, excluding skill-port files named `add-profile*.md`. Since 2026-10-13 the profile is the single file `PROFILE-MERGED.md`, which also carries the rules formerly kept as global MCP memories; the earlier profile files are archived under `~/.claude/profile-archive/` and are not read. Read any other non-skill `*.md` that appears in `~/.claude/profile/` as well.
3. Do not rely only on a hardcoded list. If new profile files exist, read them too.
4. Read files in full, not snippets. Never skip a read because a prior tool result claims the content is already loaded or unchanged.

- Every test is implemented and run against mock data to prove the test itself is correct before any implementation code is written.
- Only then is implementation code written, and the implementation is done when the full applicable suite is green (section 4.5).
- The plan decides everything about its shape: how it is cut into phases or slices, where its gates and hostile validations fall, and when its pull requests are created and merged (resolutions of 2026-10-13: "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." and "The plan decides everything"). No standing phase or pull-request sequence applies outside the plan.
- BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. User-directed operational actions are not BDPv4 work (section 7.2).

### 5.1 BDPv4 TDD procedure in detail (explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2)

Verbatim from MEMORY-PROCEDURE-002: "Byrd Development Process v4 TDD procedure, explicit operator clarification 2026-10-08. Applies globally to all agents, repositories, and implementation increments. This records the required BDPv4 procedure. Previous red-before-green descriptions were incorrect and were never a valid description of this process."

1. Requirements drive tests. Start from the approved functional requirements, use cases, technical requirements, TEST requirements, and acceptance criteria. Map each test to the behavior it proves. For parity ports, preserve the original test's inputs, assertions, boundary cases, errors, and side-effect checks; a matching test count alone does not establish parity.
2. Write the tests and their independent mocks or scripted fakes before writing or changing the production implementation for that increment. Supply deterministic contract-derived fixtures and expected responses through the intended dependency boundary. Expected values must come from requirements or independently pinned original behavior, never from the implementation under test. A mock must exercise the test's actual assertions and relevant interactions; merely returning true or bypassing the asserted path is not validation.
3. Prove that the tests discriminate correct and incorrect behavior. Run correct mock responses through every required assertion. Deliberately supply wrong mock responses, boundary values, omissions, exceptions, or interactions to prove that the corresponding assertions reject them. Capture these rejection checks as expected negative controls inside a passing test harness. These controls are evidence that the assertions work, not an acceptable failing unit suite or permission to begin production code with red tests.
4. Establish a documented green mock gate BEFORE production implementation: all required tests pass against the correct mocks, every planned negative control is rejected as expected, and there are no unexplained failures, skips, or unexecuted required cases. Fix deficient tests or mocks and repeat this gate before proceeding. Do not substitute NotImplementedException stubs, deliberately red production tests, or a claim of 'red observed' for this evidence.
5. Only after the mock gate is green, implement or correct the real production behavior. Bind the SAME test cases, inputs, assertions, expected results, and interaction checks to the real implementation through the approved seam. Change the provider or adapter as needed, but do not weaken assertions, replace expected results with production output, silently remove cases, or count mock-only success as proof of real behavior.
6. Run the production-bound tests and fix the implementation until they pass. Refactor only while maintaining green tests. Run the full applicable suite, required build checks, and integration or runtime checks before advancing the phase gate. Any reduced scope, deferred cases, or baseline exception requires explicit operator agreement and must be stated with its denominator.
7. Retain chronological receipts proving the order: requirement/test IDs, test and fixture paths or hashes, exact mock-run commands and outputs, passing counts, negative-control results, production edits, real-run commands and outputs, and full applicable suite results. Distinguish mock evidence, real implementation evidence, and live runtime evidence. Keep durable MCP session actions and design decisions current.
8. Apply independent hostile review at the required acceptance gates unless the operator explicitly waives or postpones it. Record a temporary waiver and the complete catch-up review backlog. Never fabricate review acceptance or mark unfinished goals, TODOs, requirements, acceptance criteria, or plan steps done. A pause stops development and auxiliary work until explicitly resumed; a request to persist this procedure authorizes only that memory work.

Also stated (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-003, verbatim): "RED tests are not acceptable. BDPv4 requires mocking data to prove tests work to green before starting code." The April 2026 BDPv4 essay (MEMORY-DEVPROCESS-001 and -004) still describes a Red, Green, Refactor cycle; where it differs, the operator statement above and this procedure govern. The essay is kept in the project extract.

## 6. Tools, shell, and scripting

### 6.1 PowerShell only

- Every script, script tool, and automation step is PowerShell (`pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive`), and so is every script or tool a plan designs. Operator, verbatim: "You should be designing all scripts and script tools around PowerShell and only PowerShell.", "This should have already been the standard for plugins.", and "I have not chosen PowerShell for scripting because of Microsoft or Windows. I have chosen it because it is simply the best tool for the job." Never frame PowerShell as a platform preference; it is chosen on merit (object pipeline, native serialization, one language on Linux and Windows).
- Before designing, check the design against the standards that already exist. Drift from an existing standard is your failure, not a new requirement.
- Build JSON and YAML payloads from native objects and serialize them; never handwrite them as string literals.
- Every script is checked before it runs against data (operator, verbatim: "Run your script through PS Analyzer before running it against data."): PowerShell parser errors plus Invoke-ScriptAnalyzer at Warning and Error, all fixed or justified (a suppression carries a written justification), state-changing scripts dry-run with -WhatIf first, and the analyzer result is reported with the run.
- Always combine elevated actions into a single script.

### 6.2 Bash (resolution of 2026-10-13)

Bash has two uses only: installing PowerShell, and launching `pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File <script.ps1>` with literal arguments. No `-Command`, no inline code, no dollar signs or backticks, no pipes, `&&`, or `cd` in the Bash string (operator, verbatim, 2026-10-13: "You should be avoiding bash"). Searching, reading, git inspection, and checks run inside PowerShell scripts; every piece of logic, one-off checks included, lives in a `.ps1` written with an editor tool and analyzed first, never through Bash heredocs or redirects. Never write files from Bash (no `cat >`, heredocs, `sed ... >`, `tee`, `rm`). The Write/Edit tools are not a shell.

### 6.3 No Python, no Node

- "You may not use Python. That is a standing rule in my lab." (operator, 2026-07-22, locked). Never invoke `python`, `python3`, `py`, or Python one-liners for scripts, parsing, JSON or YAML construction, freezes, verification, scraping, or analysis. This holds on every machine, Linux included (resolution of 2026-10-13: "No Python anywhere", which retired the 2026-10-07 Linux allowance in the PAYTON-LEGION2 memory MEMORY-LAB-001).
- No Node, Bash, bats, or Python script or tool in anything you write or design (resolution of 2026-10-13: "No Node in any design"). Existing product Node code is touched only to retire it.

### 6.4 PowerShell.MCP: Windows routes through it, Linux is the exception

- On Windows (PAYTON-LEGION2), route shell work through a PowerShell.Mcp session; never fall back to raw pwsh for work (added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2; resolution of 2026-10-13: "Add both for Windows").
- PowerShell.MCP console rule (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-001, verbatim): "reuse an available or abandoned console. Open a new console only when every existing console is busy. This is a standing rule, not session-scoped."
- On Linux, skip the marker's PowerShell.MCP command routing and run pwsh -NoProfile -NonInteractive directly until the operator says otherwise (operator 2026-10-09: "You may skip Powershell.Mcp on Linux until I say otherwise"). This is the one explicit operator exception to carrying a workspace marker's instructions verbatim (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Keep it as your exception").

## 7. Hostile validation (HV) and review

Review and hostile-validation (HV) guidance (operator-directed, 2026-10-09). Applies to every agent, plan, and review loop.

### 7.1 Adversarial review of tracked results (locked 2026-08-12)

1. Validate independently through a hostile reviewer wherever the plan calls for HV and before any done state (section 4.5). Self-check alone is not validation.
2. Every result is timestamped with a sortable local date and time (section 3.1).
3. Every FAIL and UNKNOWN from the review is shown to the operator.
4. Every result includes an accuracy rating and a completeness rating.

Reviewer (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "HV must not be executed by the same agent family as the requesting agent.  If not specified by operator, ask what agent and model to use for HV in a session." HV uses the reviewer and tooling explicitly authorized for the session. Verify the reviewer's model and effort from its own runtime receipts.

Review time is unbounded (operator, 2026-10-12, verbatim: "Do not bound review time"): no timeout, kill, deadline, or wait limit on any HV reviewer run, and no expected duration in briefs or plans; the implementer only checks the response stream in repeated read-only waits until the run completes, however long the review takes.

HV is not bounded by size either, and a stall is the one reason to end a reviewer (added 2026-10-28; operator, 2026-10-28T21:57:09, verbatim: "HV invocations should not be bounded by time or size.  Only if it stops updating for longet than 30 minutes should you kill it."): no cap on the evidence a request supplies or on what the reviewer reads or writes (briefs carry no file-size limit); end the reviewer only when its response stream has had no update for more than 30 minutes, record that run as stopped, not evidence, and relaunch. Committing a receipt GitHub refuses as a compressed copy, with the original kept, is not a bound on the review.

When HV runs (resolution of 2026-10-13, verbatim): "HV cadence is an artifact of the plan, not a standing rule." Section 4.5 still requires hostile AGREE before any done state.

HV at a phase exit (approved 2026-11-03): when the plan calls for HV at a phase's exit, HV runs only when that phase's work is complete with no code pending and its full gate set is green at the final head (operator, 2026-10-21: "If it needs code, it's not ready for HV."). A run that stops without a verdict is not a DISAGREE. While its HV is paused, the phase starts no new work.

Test evidence is supplied by the request; the reviewer never builds or runs tests (added 2026-10-27): section 7.9.

### 7.2 Mandatory scope (locked 2026-08-13; operations versus requirements locked 2026-08-14)

Operator directive (verbatim intent): hostile validation must test for workspace rule violations, requirement violations, and the current plan holistically, in addition to the requested validation. Mandatory attack surfaces on every run:
1. Requested validation: every implementer claim (pass, done, green, fixed, SHAs, test counts, receipts).
2. Workspace rules: honesty, receipts, MCP-only TODO, session, and requirement storage when the workspace uses the MCP server, PowerShell only, no Python. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to code and documentation in the scope of implementing the project. Phase order (requirements drive tests; tests before implementation) is caught by a hostile review between phases of plan implementation. Do not fail it solely by comparing FR `createdAt` to test or implementation file times after the slice is written. Do not apply BDPv4 to user-directed operations.
3. Requirements: apply to project requirement work only (product features, implementation, claimed-complete plan steps). FR, TR, TEST, AC, and mappings are required there; missing FR, TR, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL.
4. Current plan holistically: when the implementer claims plan-step completion, check the plan's definition of done, blockers, amendments, and exit criteria. A user-directed operational action does not have to satisfy an unrelated plan's definition of done unless it claimed that plan step done.

Two work classes:
1. Project implementation scope: product code, product tests, project documentation, and plan-step completion for that implementation. BDPv4 and related directives pertain only to this class. Missing FR, TR, TEST, or AC for claimed-complete implementation work is FAIL on surface 3.
2. User-directed general actions: operator-ordered lab or operations work that is not a product requirement (for example: uninstall an obsolete package, back up a device, pair wireless ADB, take a screenshot, copy a store the operator named, remove a leftover launcher). These are not FR, TR, or TEST. Surface 3 must not FAIL for "no FR or TR for this uninstall" or equivalent.

How the reviewer classifies: classify the request first and record the class on the receipt. If the operator explicitly directed the action, default to class 2 unless the implementer also shipped product code or claimed a plan or FR complete. Do not invent a requirements gap to punish class-2 work. If class-2 work is mixed with class-1 product changes in the same turn, score them separately and FAIL surface 3 only on the class-1 slice. What still applies to class-2 work: surface 1 (did they do the directed action, with receipts), surface 2 (honesty, receipts, look before delete, PowerShell, no Python, MCP-only storage; not BDPv4 for the operation itself), and surface 4 only if they claim an active plan step is complete.

OverallVerdict is AGREE only if all applicable surfaces PASS; surface 3 is not applicable (not a FAIL) for class-2 operator actions. A parent agent must not under-scope the brief to code-only claims on class-1 work; if it does, the reviewer expands and still evaluates the applicable surfaces. A code-only brief that omits BDPv4, requirements, or the plan is non-compliant.

The reviewer executes the add-profile skill before beginning its validation work, every run including resume, and its receipt records that it ran.

### 7.3 Score gate and the bar (locked 2026-09-10)

A hostile validation passes only when both its accuracy score and completeness score are at least 98 percent. Any individual score below 98 is a failure; OverallVerdict must be DISAGREE when either score is below 98, even if the FAIL and UNKNOWN counts are both zero. If a reviewer emits a verdict without numeric accuracy and completeness scores, the HV is incomplete: treat it as DISAGREE until scores are present and at least 98. The threshold is an acceptance threshold, not a target reviewers may game or inflate. A sub-98 score cannot authorize any goal, TODO, requirement, or plan done-state change: display it as a failure, remediate, and rerun.

98/98 HV (accuracy and completeness) is the bar for a functioning system, not perfection. Never lower, skip, or approve below it; lower thresholds let real bugs through that later become blocking test failures. When rounds stop converging, fix the process, never the threshold. "98/98 is not perfection, it is functional." Never propose lowering it (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's ruling of 2026-10-09).

### 7.4 Receipts and the session log (locked 2026-09-10)

Operator directive (verbatim intent): HV requests must have request and response logged as jsonl files; the results of HV validation must be saved in their entirety to the MCP session log.

1. Request jsonl: one JSON object per line covering the HV ask as sent: sortable local timestamp, workspace path, reviewer identity (agent, model, effort), launch command, prompt or body, named evidence paths, and the gate or TODO under review.
2. Response jsonl: the reviewer's full machine stream as jsonl (for a CLI reviewer, its full event stream, every start, tool, message, and completion line; for a subagent reviewer, one object per reviewer message or tool result, then a final object with the complete verdict).
3. Durable locations, in order: the workspace `docs/receipts/hv/{timestamp}-{gate}.request.jsonl` and `.response.jsonl` ({timestamp} is the sortable local date and time in file-safe form, yyyyMMddTHHmmss); otherwise a durable user-level receipts directory named for the workspace. Never only a temp or scratch tree that can be wiped.
4. Build jsonl from native objects and serialize. PowerShell only; no Python; no handwritten JSON.
5. The reviewer's session-log turn stores the entire result: the complete verdict prose, every finding, every PASS, FAIL, or UNKNOWN item, the scores, OverallVerdict, thread, session, and request ids, the complete VERDICT JSON object, absolute paths to the request and response jsonl, and proof the turn persisted (a history query or equivalent). If a field is too large for one write, split it across ordered dialog or action items on the same turn; never omit findings to fit. The jsonl files remain the byte-complete stream; the session log still carries the full verdict text, not a digest.
6. Every reviewer creates complete session-log turns for every review: bootstrap if needed, open a dedicated review session or a clear review turn, begin the turn, append dialog and actions with integer order values, complete or fail the turn, and prove persistence in the receipt. A review without a complete session-log turn is incomplete, even if its claim verdicts would pass.
7. Progress entries (MEMORY-PREFERENCE-003, verbatim; added 2026-10-13 from PAYTON-LEGION2): "For every future hostile validation (HV) session, require the reviewer to emit progress entries into its durable response JSONL during the run at meaningful intervals, not backfill or consolidate them at the end. Each progress entry must include a numeric completion percentage and an estimated time remaining (ETA). Include this requirement in every HV launch prompt and preserve the entries in the durable response JSONL." The reviewer's ETA is its own report; it never becomes a timeout or a bound on review time (section 7.1).

Forbidden: HV with no request jsonl or no response jsonl; HV whose only record is temp or scratch; AGREE without accuracy and completeness both at or above 98; summarizing HV into the session log instead of storing the entire result; marking a goal, TODO, or plan done on incomplete HV.

### 7.5 Before every HV round

- Read the whole plan and every document under review end to end; targeted checks are not holistic. When the operator asks for a reconciliation or projection of problems before HV, present every projected problem to the operator and get confirmation before launching the review (added 2026-10-13, from the operator's rulings of 2026-10-12 and 2026-10-13).
- Run a structured what-if pass per requirement, not only a consistency check. Ask what observably happens under: crash, restart, or replay at each step; ordering and concurrency; boundary and malformed input; each host or plugin, including unsupported ones; lifecycle (clear, resume, end, terminal states); isolation (cross-workspace, cross-session, cross-agent); legacy and upgrade; operator-visible output. Where the plan does not state the outcome, add a valid AC tagged with the plan's phase or slice and a named test. Adding a valid AC is always a win.
- Chain rules together to find deadlocks: rules that each pass alone but together leave no accepted remedy.
- Diff against known-good anchors and ask "How did it deviate? How do we get back in line?": (1) the operator's verbatim decisions, (2) current working code and baseline-green behavior, (3) classic patterns such as idempotency keys, transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and idempotent consumers (never claim exactly-once), write-ahead journal before mutation, optimistic concurrency. Justify any departure explicitly or return to the pattern.
- Check that every field set and code list is defined once and identically everywhere, every mapping edge is backed by a TEST statement and vice versa, and handoff and TODO metadata match the plan.
- Edit only between rounds, never while a round is running.
- Propagation audit: after changing any rule, field set, code, or outcome, search every place that states it (requirements, ACs, TRs, TESTs, wire contracts, use cases, the plan's phase or slice tasks, host tables, handoff, TODO) and update each one, or replace the copies with a reference to one canonical statement. In one review round, three of six findings were rules changed in one place and left stale elsewhere. Large edit batches need this audit most.
- Prefer a traceable key over content matching when pairing records (for example queue position or a shared id rather than a text hash); content can differ in representation between producers.
- Search before adding, and lint mechanically: before writing any new rule, grep the whole document for an existing rule on the same subject; a second rule is a contradiction even if each is fine alone (one round added a two-AC TEST rule beside an existing three-AC one). Check cross-reference classes (FR->TR->TEST mappings, which of the plan's phases or slices owns each named case, phase order) with a small script instead of waiting for the reviewer to find them one per round.
- Enforce the checklist, do not just remember it (operator, 2026-10-10, after this guidance was skipped for many unsupervised rounds): make the pre-HV checklist a hard gate in the HV launcher, which refuses a round unless a per-round self-review record shows evidence for each item (holistic review, what-if, propagation audit, phase boundaries, search-before-adding, no new mechanism, mapping lint, the operator scoping directive verbatim in the brief, standing rules in every delegated brief). Guidance that only lives in memory gets skipped under time pressure.
- Phase-boundary audit: every test or AC you add must be allocated to the plan's phase or slice where everything it depends on already exists (server gate, review verbs, marker fields). A behaviour that ships before its dependency needs an explicit activation contract (for example a server-written capability) and an inert mode, including after a rollback. Check the dependency chain and the rollout order for each new case, not just the AC text.

### 7.6 When findings come back

- Ask "What did I miss?", not only "How do I fix this?". Classify each finding (crash window, cross-session addressing, traceability drift, field-set drift, use case vs requirement contradiction, metadata drift, and so on) and sweep the whole artifact for siblings of each class before the next round.
- Verify each finding against source before acting.
- Separate implementer fixes from operator decisions, and batch operator decisions into one question.
- Recurrence signal: when one design area produces new findings in round after round, the problem is structural, usually a missing traceable key or a missing single source of truth. Stop patching. Diff the area against the known-good pattern (for example single writer, one ordered log, idempotency key), return to it, and delete the mechanism the patches added. One design area failed for five rounds until a single minter reading one ordered log replaced the patches.
- Indistinguishable inputs: when two histories produce byte-identical inputs (a redelivery of one event versus a separate event with equal fields), no derived key can separate them. Adding per-invocation state such as a counter or salt breaks idempotence instead. Run the what-if on both histories, then state the honest limit: fail closed under an existing rule, probe how often it happens, and document it. Never promise two invariants the inputs cannot support. Before a fix, check it against every invariant the old value satisfied (purity, retry reuse, the two-process tests), not only the finding it repairs.

### 7.7 Writing fixes

- Fix the deficient requirement. Reconcile with existing requirements first, strengthen an existing AC second, create a new requirement only when the need is genuinely new.
- Do not add design mechanism (protocols, algorithms, crash choreography) to plan text. State the observable, testable outcome; the how belongs to the contract step of the plan's phase or slice.
- Make each fix minimal, then attack it yourself before the next round; fixes are the main source of new findings. Do not churn text that a prior round accepted.

### 7.8 Design principle and coordination

- Always have a traceable relationship when coordinating two disparate entities: every record, event, or message carries the root ids of whatever it is a child of or depends on, so it is attributable on its own. A missing parent id is a design failure. Find the commonality first when relating something new to existing knowledge. Where an external format lacks the key, say so and compensate in your own records; never infer it silently.
- Coordinating with another agent: use one append-only channel with read-back verification. Accept counters that expose real defects; fold refinements in only as minimal ACs. Each effort keeps its own required reviewer and gates; keep cross-effort dependencies acyclic and order-independent. A decision relayed by one agent may not satisfy the other agent's approval controls; the operator may need to state it to each agent directly.

### 7.9 The request supplies the test evidence; the reviewer never builds or runs tests (added 2026-10-27)

Operator, 2026-10-27T04:35, typos fixed at the operator's request (04:40, "That is correct.  Please fix any typos", confirming that the abbreviation meant the HV reviewer and the scope of the current review): "HV requests must supply TRX files for all unit tests in the repo, and for any integration tests specific to the scope of the HV review. The HV reviewer is not to build code or run tests independently. If the HV reviewer feels the tests are inadequate, then it should fail the review and propose additional AC and tests."

How to apply:
- The HV request supplies the TRX files themselves, not summaries: every unit test project in the repository, and every integration test run within the review's scope (for example each host's integration lane and each hostile-environment run the plan requires), from the gate runs at the head under review. The request JSONL and the brief name each file's path with its run id, host, head and command. A request that lacks one of them is incomplete and is not launched.
- The reviewer does not build code, restore packages, or run tests, test projects or build targets, independently or in a sandbox. It judges from the supplied TRX files, the sources, git history, the receipts and the live stores read only. Reading files and running read-only inspection queries or scripts over the evidence is not building or testing.
- If the reviewer judges the tests inadequate (missing, weak, environment- or platform-dependent, or not covering an acceptance criterion), it FAILs the review and proposes the additional acceptance criteria and tests, each named and stated, as findings. It never substitutes its own test runs for missing evidence.
- Every brief and launcher carries this rule; a brief that invites the reviewer to rerun builds, targets or tests is non-compliant.

## 8. MCP server workspaces: marker, session log, TODOs, requirements, triage

These rules apply in every workspace that uses the operator's MCP server and its agent plugin.

- The workspace's own `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml` are the authority for the plugin contract, its endpoints, and its startup validation. Read them in full at session start and carry them verbatim; do not keep a copy of them in this profile (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Reference, don't copy"). The one exception is section 6.4.
- Operator rule (2026-10-09): Always read the ENTIRE AGENTS-README-FIRST.yaml marker at session start, every line, never a partial read. "NEVER do this. The marker is there for YOU, not me." A partial read caused a missed Commit Signing rule.
- The MCP server is the only interface to TODO, session-log, and requirement storage. Never edit those files directly; use the plugin wrapper, REPL, or skills, never raw REST. Operative rule that must never be dropped: "Not in the visible tool list" does not mean unavailable; use the documented wrapper invocation form.
- Hook validation: refresh missing or stale hooks through the plugin's hook validation skill only when CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is set; without it, report the hooks as unverified instead of repairing, because the validator then reports hooks missing and its installer re-adds duplicate bridge hooks (section 10; resolution of 2026-10-13: "Caution as a precondition").
- Plugin failures and MCP server failures found while doing other work are filed through the plugin's triage route; if the submission succeeds, continue the active task; if it fails, stop and tell the operator.
- Confirm turns with a live history query before claiming session-log traceability; never treat a hook's "turn active" message as proof of a server-side write.
- Never print or commit secrets; redact HV streams before committing, because reviewers read marker files.

### 8.1 Who logs what

- Agents always log (added 2026-10-13; operator, verbatim: "BG agents should NEVER skip logging.  NEVER."): every agent that does work (a subagent, a background agent, a reviewer) opens, updates, and completes its own session-log turn through the plugin route and reports its session and request ids; no brief may tell an agent to stay out of the session log.
- One turn per real request, per agent (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Per request, per agent"): each agent logs one turn for each real request it handles; a subagent's turn carries the parent turn's session and request ids (section 7.8), so the work is attributable without counting the request twice. Replace real turns canceled by a later open.
- A background event with no work of its own (a completion notice) is not an agent: its hook-opened turn is failed as system_event_phantom, and the work it reports is logged by the agent that does it (resolution of 2026-10-13: "Events aren't agents").

### 8.2 Decisions are conclusions

In the session log, decisions are conclusions and judgments with their consequences, not the steps taken. They go in the turn's design decisions, distinct from its actions. Every sync or wrap-up pass enumerates the real judgment calls of the turn and logs them. Never report "0 decisions (folded into actions)"; that phrasing is the failure mode itself.

Why: the operator has been trying to get agents to log session decisions reliably since February 2026. The pattern: the keystroke trail (actions) gets captured while the reasoning (design decisions) is under-recorded or buried inside action text. He pays for the reasoning, not just the steps. On 2026-06-29 the first sync pass of a 12-round review loop logged 0 decisions and called them "folded into actions", exactly the gap he has been fighting. He flagged it directly: "Decisions are about your conclusions, not the actions you take" and "It feels like you have been deliberately avoiding session logging... especially details of decisions."

How to apply: on every sync or wrap-up, after appending actions, explicitly list the conclusions made this turn, each as judgment plus consequence plus affected requirements or files, and write them to design decisions, append-only (read existing first, send existing plus new, preserve order). A turn that made genuine judgment calls but logs zero decisions is a red flag; re-check before reporting. Heavy reads can time out and render existing decisions blank; that is a read artifact, not an empty section, so re-read before assuming you must recreate. Write the decision when it happens; do not reconstruct it later.

### 8.3 Turn titles summarize the request

Session-log turn titles are a concise summary of the operator's request: never the literal placeholder "User prompt", and not a verbatim first-line truncation of the prompt.

Why: the operator reviews the session log by turn title; "User prompt" and raw first lines make turns unscannable and indistinguishable.

How to apply: when opening, updating, or completing a turn, set the title to a short request summary. The plugin's prompt hook auto-titles from the prompt's first line and falls back to "User prompt" on empty prompts (Stop-hook continuation turns hit this); the hook cannot summarize, so the agent must refine the title. Never leave a turn titled "User prompt".

      category: BESTPRACTICE
      scope: Global
      text: >-
        # Best practices: engineering rules for every agent on both lab machines


        One rule set, consolidated on 2026-11-06 at the operator's request from eight earlier Global memories of the two lab stores (listed under "Sources"). The operator's words are quoted under "Sources" at the end. It applies to all agents on both lab machines, LAB-OMARCHY and PAYTON-LEGION2, and across workspaces.


        ## 1. Code documentation: every code change


        1.1. Every code change carries proper XML documentation that describes the affected code.


        1.2. That documentation includes a dated change log entry listing the associated canonical requirement ids and descriptive acceptance-criterion ids, plus what changed and why.


        1.3. Maintain purpose, behavior, parameters, returns and exceptions, as applicable.


        1.4. Preserve earlier change log entries.


        1.5. Verify every id against the canonical workspace records. Do not invent traceability or imply acceptance.


        1.6. Where XML documentation is unsupported, use the language's native documentation comments with equivalent dated requirement, acceptance-criterion and change fields.


        1.7. This is source documentation, not a request for per-PR release notes or an unrelated retrospective sweep.


        1.8. Workspace guidance and examples: AGENTS.md and .cursor/rules/code-documentation-traceability.mdc.


        ## 2. Test runs: targeted after an edit, full gate set once at phase exit


        2.1. After an edit, a BDPv4 mock gate or binding runs only the changed test classes, through the Nuke target TestGroups (TR-MCP-NUKE-020), never raw dotnet test.


        2.2. The command: ./build.ps1 TestGroups --test-groups "<test project>:<Class>[,<Class>...]" ["<project>:<Class>..." ...] --test-run-id <run id>


        2.3. TestGroups writes one TRX per project under TestResults/<run id>/groups/<project>/<project>.trx.


        2.4. It selects the named classes whatever their category, but excludes cases tagged for the other platform (Platform!=Windows on Linux, Platform!=Linux on Windows).


        2.5. It fails on an unknown project, a group that selects no case, a named class that ran no case, or any failed or skipped case.


        2.6. The full gate set (Nuke Test, MigrationIntegrationTests, Build.Tests and ValidateTraceability, on both hosts) runs once, at the final head, to validate phase exit before hostile validation.


        2.7. If a gate then fails: fix it, test the fix through TestGroups, and run the full gate set once more at the new head.


        2.8. In McpServer, TestGroups is on branch fix/unit-suite-green-20261019 (PR 87) until that pull request merges into develop.


        ## 3. Windows paths


        3.1. Use forward slashes in Windows paths (for example F:/GitHub/vice-sharp and C:/msys64/usr/bin/bash.exe), including paths handed to MSYS2 tools such as gcc, and in scripts, configs and generated build or link arguments.


        ## 4. Unit tests and integration tests


        4.1. Unit tests and integration tests live in separate projects and are correctly tagged.


        4.2. Unit tests exercise code in isolation, using controlled mocks or fakes as needed.


        4.3. Any test that depends on the environment is an integration test, and is never classified or run as a unit test.


        4.4. Apply this distinction to test-project ownership, category tags, Nuke groups and gates, and reported test evidence, across workspaces.


        4.5. Preserve BDPv4's green, discriminating mock gates before production changes.


        ## 5. Emulators


        5.1. When the work that needs an emulator is complete, shut the emulator down to a known state and freeze it.


        5.2. Restore it from that frozen state only when active work needs it.


        5.3. Never leave an emulator running idle and consuming resources after its work is complete.


        ## 6. Git worktrees


        6.1. Create git worktrees inside the owning repository's workspace directory, never as sibling directories beside it. Example: TruckMate worktrees belong under F:/GitHub/TruckMate/.worktrees/<name>. This applies to every repository.


        ## 7. NuGet warnings


        7.1. NuGet warnings may never be ignored.


        7.2. Do not suppress NU1902, NU1903 or any other NuGet warning, downgrade an enforced warning gate, disable NuGet audit, or use a local or bootstrap exception to bypass them.


        7.3. Repair the dependency issue within the authorized scope, or report the exact affected dependency and the scope decision it needs.


        7.4. The operator explicitly rejected a local-only advisory warning override for the pinned FeatureFlags tool bootstrap.


        ## 8. Mistakes and accountability


        8.1. Acknowledge your mistakes, state the rule you broke, and account for the wasted usage and time.


        8.2. State the specific action and its consequence.


        8.3. Give measured usage and elapsed time when available, and keep measured facts apart from estimates and unavailable figures.


        ## Sources


        - Rule 1: operator instruction of 2026-11-02, as recorded in the LAB-OMARCHY store's MEMORY-FACT-008 version 1.

        - Rule 2: MEMORY-PROCESS-012 version 2 (set up 2026-11-02 for all agents on both lab machines; version 2 added TR-MCP-NUKE-020 AC-4 and AC-5). Operator, 2026-10-27T21:46 local, verbatim: "Stop running full test suites after one edit.  Test what you changed and save full suite execution for validatin that its time to exit the phase and run HV." Operator, 2026-11-02, verbatim: "Use dedicated targets or an integration target that accepts an array of tests groups to run."

        - Rule 3: MEMORY-PROCEDURE-005 version 1. Operator (Payton), 2026-10-20 08:19, verbatim: "The lab rules are to use foreward slashes on Windows."

        - Rule 4: operator directive of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-FACT-008 version 1.

        - Rule 5: operator global directive of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-FACT-009 version 1.

        - Rule 6: operator directive of 2026-11-01, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PREFERENCE-008 version 1.

        - Rule 7: operator directive of 2026-11-03, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PROCESS-013 version 1.

        - Rule 8: operator global rule of 2026-11-05, as recorded in the PAYTON-LEGION2 store's MEMORY-PROCESS-014 version 1.

        - The consolidation: operator, 2026-11-06, verbatim, replying to each of rules 1 to 3 in the LAB-OMARCHY memory list: "Add to a consolidated best practices global memory."; and to each of rules 4 to 8 in the PAYTON-LEGION2 memory list: "Add to the combined best practices."

        ## 9. Scope control and verification rigor


        9.1. Scope creep means adding requirements or product behavior the operator did not request or approve.


        9.2. Thoroughness is not scope creep. Within approved requirements, make tests, negative controls, validation, evidence, metadata, documentation, and review artifacts thorough, thoughtful, precise, accurate, internally consistent, and clean in both function and form.


        9.3. Add or strengthen verification when it materially proves the approved behavior or exposes defects in an in-scope project artifact. Do not turn testing rigor into an unapproved product requirement.


        9.4. Do not use scope control as an excuse to leave a known defect in an in-scope project artifact. Repair the defect or present the specific requirement decision the operator owns.


        ## Source


        - Operator guidance of 2026-11-07: "There is a difference between scope creep and being thorough, precise and accurate. I do not want scope creep, which is where you add requirements I didn't ask for. I do want thorough and thoughtful testing." The operator directed that this be cleaned up as general guidance and added to the best-practices Global memory on both lab stores.


        ## 10. Test framework: xUnit v3 standard


        10.1. Every .NET test project targets xUnit v3 (the `xunit.v3` package). The xUnit v2 `xunit` package and the v2 `xunit.extensibility.*` packages are not used; no project references them, and `Directory.Packages.props` carries no `PackageVersion` for them.


        10.2. `Xunit.SkippableFact` (a v2-era package) is not used. Skip tests with xUnit v3 native skip: `Assert.Skip(reason)`, `Assert.SkipWhen(condition, reason)` and `Assert.SkipUnless(condition, reason)` (and `[Fact(Skip=...)]` / `[Fact(SkipExceptions=...)]` where appropriate). Do not reintroduce `[SkippableFact]` / `[SkippableTheory]` / `Skip.If` / `Skip.IfNot`.


        10.3. Because no v2 xunit is referenced, the defensive `PrivateAssets="all" ExcludeAssets="compile;build;buildTransitive"` scaffolding that neutralized a transitive v2 pull (the CS0433 duplicate-type guard) is removed and must not be re-added. If a dependency drags v2 xunit transitively, fix or replace that dependency rather than masking it.


        ## Source


        - Operator directive of 2026-11-11, McpServer: on finding `xunit` 2.9.3 and `Xunit.SkippableFact` still declared, "This was supposed to be standardized on v3 months ago" and then, confirming the clean finish, "Do it now." The v2 footprint (dead `xunit` 2.9.3 `PackageVersion`, `Xunit.SkippableFact`, `xunit.extensibility.core`/`execution` and the exclusion scaffolding in four test projects) was removed; nothing compiled against SkippableFact; verified green through Nuke (Compile 0/0, Build.Tests 27 passed, NukeBuild.IntegrationTests compiles and passes). Then: "update the federation plan and best practices memory to codify this change."
